avoid: Extended periods of sitting perfectly still
children.game_version: A 'copy-cat' game where the leader makes up a funny line and the children repeat it with a clap.

seniors.seated_version: Naturally seated; can be performed in standard chairs if cross-legged is difficult.
seniors.standing_version: Not recommended as the tradition is fundamentally seated.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce clapping speed; limit torso swaying to a comfortable range.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Rhythmic clapping and synchronized arm gestures to emphasize the beat
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Groups of 10-15 sitting in rows or a semi-circle on a stage
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Rhythmic body movements and swaying while seated

signature_moves.description: Synchronized rhythmic hand-clapping performed by the entire chorus
signature_moves.name: Awak-awak clapping

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Starts low-key and builds to high-energy rhythmic intensity
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Individual improvisation during chorus segments; movements must be in perfect unison

music_profile.musical_form: Two segments: complex musical intro (tok juara) followed by improvised pantuns (tukang karut)
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Responsorial singing with percussive clapping and rebana beats
music_profile.sound_description: A percussive vocal tradition where a lead singer's improvised melodic lines are immediately echoed by a powerful, rhythmic unison chorus, punctuated by sharp hand-claps and the deep resonance of the rebana drum.
music_profile.vocal_style: Responsorial, unison chorus, improvised solo verses

basic_steps: Sit cross-legged on a flat platform in a tight group formation
Perform rhythmic hand-clapping in unison with the chorus
Execute synchronized torso swaying and shoulder movements
Listen to the tukang karut's improvised line
Sing the line back in responsorial unison
teaching.formation: Seated group (10-15 members) sitting cross-legged on a platform
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start as 'awak-awak' (chorus members) focusing on rhythm and unison singing.
teaching.rhythm: Percussive and syncopated, driven by hand-claps and rebana
